blocks.text: By the end of this lesson you'll be able to tap a steady beat with clicks, counting out loud, and you'll have tried keeping it going on your own. Next lesson the beat gets notes of different lengths.

# Last time
Before anything new, a quick warm-up from lesson 1. Tap **Start** to play the copying game: watch which black keys light up, listen, and play the pattern back. A pattern of three is plenty; it's just to get your hands back on the groups.

blocks.title: Warm-up: copy black-key patterns
blocks.about: Copy the black-key patterns from lesson 1: a pattern of three is plenty.

blocks.text:
# What the beat is
Music has a **beat**: a steady pulse underneath it, like your footsteps when you walk or your heartbeat. In some music it's quick, in some it's slow, and the notes are measured against it. When you tap your foot to a song without thinking, you're tapping the beat. For now we'll practise keeping the beat perfectly steady; later you'll meet music that speeds up or slows down on purpose.

# Feel it first
Play the music below: the opening of Michael Jackson's *Billie Jean*. It starts with the drums on their own, and their beat is very clear. Stand up and walk in place to it, one step on each beat. Then sit and tap your thighs with both hands, one tap on each beat. When that feels settled, count along out loud: "1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4…", one number on each beat. Like a great many songs, this one groups its beats in fours.

Counting aloud feels odd at first. Keep at it: it's what will keep you steady when you play.

If the video won't play, put on any song with a strong, steady beat, or open the metronome (Practice → Metronome) and walk and tap with its clicks.

blocks.title: Michael Jackson, Billie Jean (the opening)
blocks.caption: Walk, then tap your thighs, then count 1 to 4 with the beat.

blocks.text:
# Before you tap: a quick timing check
Every phone or tablet takes a moment to turn a sound into something you hear, and a moment to notice your tap. Bluetooth headphones add more. So the first time you open a rhythm drill, the app offers a short timing check: it plays eight clicks and you tap along. It uses the result to judge your taps fairly from then on. Say yes, tap as evenly as you can, and if you ever change headphones or devices, run it again from Settings.

# Tap with the clicks
When you tap **Start**, you'll see a big pad where the keys usually are, and it makes a short sound when you tap it. First the app plays the beat, lighting the pad on each one. Then it counts you in with four clicks (1, 2, 3, 4) and keeps clicking while you tap. From here the pad stays dark, so listen for the clicks. Press the pad on every click and keep your finger down until just before the next one, counting out loud: press, hold, let go, press. Every note on the pad lasts as long as your finger stays down. In this drill each note lasts one beat: press on the click, hold, and let go just before the next click. Holding for most of the beat is what counts; a quick dab is "let go early".

With a keyboard plugged in, any key works as the pad.

Aim to press **exactly with** the click, so that your tap's sound and the click land together as one. If you hear two separate sounds, a tap and a click, you're a little early or late. Don't chase the click; keep your pressing even and let it settle onto the clicks. The app is lenient about timing in this lesson; it gets a little stricter later.

blocks.title: Tap with the clicks
blocks.about: Press the pad on every click, hold until just before the next, and count out loud.

blocks.text:
# Keep it going on your own
Now try it with no clicks while you tap, and the pad doesn't light. The app plays the beat once so you can hear its speed. Then you start when you're ready (your first tap starts it) and keep tapping at that speed, counting out loud. The usual thing is to speed up a little without noticing; counting aloud helps. This one is just to try: keeping the beat on your own comes back in the lessons ahead.

blocks.title: Keep the beat on your own
blocks.about: Listen to the beat once, then keep it going on your own, counting out loud.

blocks.text:
# Check yourself
- Tap your thighs to the *Billie Jean* opening again without counting. Did you stay with it?
- Count "1, 2, 3, 4" aloud and tap a steady beat on your thigh for a minute, no music. Did you speed up?
- In the drill, did your tap and the click sound as one, or as two?

# If this happens
- **The app says you're late (or early) every time, by about the same amount, though you were with the click.** Run the timing check again (Settings), especially after changing headphones; Bluetooth adds delay.
- **You speed up without the clicks.** Count aloud, and listen to your counting rather than your fingers.
- **The app says "let go early".** Keep your finger down until just before the next beat: a press, not a dab.
- **A tap doesn't seem to register.** Press with the pad of your finger, and lift fully between notes.
